title: Proof 7: orthodox antiquity and pagan witnesses — Cap. 9 close
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): SEVENTH, by ye consensus plus authority belonging toward orthodox antiquity. Dionysius (On ye Divine Names, chapter 5): Unity, he says, God according to His supersubstantial simple infinity contains. Damascene (Orthodox Faith 1.12): Ye universe, he says, that which is, as a certain immense plus infinite sea belonging toward essence in His embrace He contains. Bernard: For God this to be is, which all these things to be is. Mercury Trismegistus God ye interminable plus infinite Good calls. Orpheus God ye infinite end calls. So Xenophanes, Parmenides, Melissus say that that which is — namely God — infinite is.
pass_b_english: SEVENTH, by the consensus and authority of orthodox antiquity. Dionysius (On the Divine Names, chapter 5): Unity, he says, God contains according to His supersubstantial simple infinity. Damascene (Orthodox Faith 1.12): The universe, he says, that which is, as a certain immense and infinite sea of essence He contains in His embrace. Bernard: For God this is to be, which is to be all these things. Mercury Trismegistus calls God the interminable and infinite Good. Orpheus calls God the infinite end. So Xenophanes, Parmenides, Melissus say that that which is — namely God — is infinite.
source_text: SEPTIMO, consensu & autoritate orthodoxae antiquitatis. Dionysius libro de divinis nominibus cap. 5: Unitas, ait, continet Deus, secundum supersubstantialem simplicem infinitatem suam. Damascenus lib. 1. orthod. fidei cap. 12: Universum, ait, id quod est, tanquam immensum quoddam & infinitum essentiae pelagus complexu suo continet. Bernhardus: Hoc Deo est esse, quod haec omnia esse. Mercurius Trismegistus Deum vocat Bonum interminatum & infinitum. Orpheus Deum appellat infinitum finem. Sic Xenophanes, Parmenides, Melissus dicunt, id quod est, nempe Deum, infinitum esse.
